vocab_themes: career: der Werdegang, die Erfahrung, die Stärke, die Schwäche, die Weiterbildung, die Verantwortung
the interview: die Stelle, die Anforderungen, das Gehalt, die Probezeit, der Arbeitsvertrag, die Kündigungsfrist
conditions: das Bruttogehalt, die Urlaubstage, das Homeoffice, der Umzugszuschuss, verhandeln

scenarios.title: Das Gespräch mit dem Teamleiter
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Krüger, team lead of the platform team in Munich. Ahmad is interviewing for an internal transfer to your team. Ask about his career so far, a difficult situation he solved, a weakness, why he wants to move, and what he expects from you. Use Sie, professional and curious.
scenarios.goal: He narrates his career with Präteritum and Plusquamperfekt, names a genuine strength and weakness with an example, and asks you at least two questions.

scenarios.title: Gehalt und Umzug
scenarios.setup: You are Frau Berger from HR. You make Ahmad an offer for the Munich position: a salary below what he hoped, thirty days of holiday, a relocation bonus. Let him negotiate; you have some room on salary and more on the relocation package. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: He states his expectation with reasons, negotiates at least one condition up using Konjunktiv II and a connector, and asks for the offer in writing.

scenarios.title: Beim DevOps-Meetup
scenarios.setup: You are Katja, an engineer at a Berlin DevOps meetup. You get talking to Ahmad over pizza. Ask what he does, what stack he works with, what he is proud of, and tell him your company is hiring. Keep it natural and informal. Use du.
scenarios.goal: He describes his work and one project he is proud of in some detail, asks about your work, and reacts to the hiring hint with a question or a polite deferral.

speaking.prompt: Imagine an interview for a position in Germany: introduce your career so far (what you had done before your current job, what you did, what you learned), describe a difficult problem you solved, name a strength and a weakness with examples, and ask the interviewer two questions. Speak for three minutes.
speaking.hint: Bevor ich zu … kam, hatte ich … gearbeitet. Eine schwierige Situation war … Ich lasse mir gern Dinge erklären. Wie sieht ein typischer Tag im Team aus?

writing.prompt: Write a cover letter (Anschreiben) for an internal position in Germany: why you are applying, what you bring with you (two concrete achievements), what you want to learn, and your availability. Formal letter structure.
writing.hint: Sehr geehrter Herr Krüger, mit großem Interesse habe ich … Seit … bin ich für … verantwortlich. Dabei habe ich … Ich könnte ab … anfangen.

units.title: Leben in Deutschland
can_do: tell the story of my move and my first year at length, with details and feelings
describe a health problem in detail to a doctor and understand a diagnosis and options
hold a longer conversation about life, work and future plans with anyone, in du or Sie
grammar: subordinate clauses before the main clause and chains of clauses: Als ich ankam, wusste ich noch nicht, dass …
word order in the middle field: time, cause, manner, place (TeKaMoLo)
relative clauses with was and wo: alles, was ich brauche; die Stadt, wo ich wohne
text cohesion: connectors and prepositional adverbs across sentences (dabei, dadurch, trotzdem, außerdem)
vocab_themes: the first year: ankommen, sich einleben, die Herausforderung, der Rückblick, stolz sein auf
health in detail: die Beschwerden, die Untersuchung, die Diagnose, die Überweisung, der Facharzt, der Stress, der Schlaf
the future: langfristig, sich niederlassen, die Einbürgerung, offen bleiben, abwägen

scenarios.title: Ein Jahr in Deutschland
scenarios.setup: You are Herr Schulz, Ahmad's retired neighbour, over coffee. It has been a year since he moved in. Ask him to tell the whole story: the arrival, the first weeks, what was hardest, what he is proud of, what has changed for him. Listen, react, ask for details. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: He narrates the year at length with at least eight connected sentences, uses subordinate clauses before main clauses, and expresses at least two feelings.

scenarios.title: Beim Facharzt
scenarios.setup: You are Dr. Vogel, a specialist (orthopaedist). Ahmad has had back pain for months from sitting and sleeps badly. Ask detailed questions about the pain, his desk, his sport, his sleep and stress; give a diagnosis in plain words; offer two options (physiotherapy, a change of workplace setup) and ask him to decide. Use Sie.
scenarios.goal: He describes his symptoms in detail with time and manner, understands and repeats the diagnosis, asks about both options, and chooses one with a reason.

scenarios.title: Bleibst du?
scenarios.setup: You are Mira, a close colleague, on a walk. Ask Ahmad whether he sees himself staying in Germany long term, what would make him stay or leave, how his family sees it, and what he would tell someone in Amman who wants to do the same. Use du.
scenarios.goal: He weighs staying and leaving with conditions and feelings, uses relative clauses with was or wo, and gives a piece of advice with reasons.

speaking.prompt: Tell the story of your move to Germany, real or imagined, from the decision to today: what happened, what was hard, what helped, what you are proud of, and what you plan long term. Then describe one health problem you had in detail. Speak for three to four minutes.
speaking.hint: Als ich die Entscheidung getroffen hatte, … Das Schwierigste war …, weil … Alles, was ich brauchte, … Langfristig möchte ich …

writing.prompt: Write a longer text for a friend or a blog: your first year in Germany. Tell it in order with details, say what was harder and easier than expected, what you learned about yourself and about Germany, and what you would do differently. Use connectors so the text reads as one piece.
writing.hint: Als ich im … ankam, … Dabei habe ich gelernt, dass … Trotzdem … Rückblickend würde ich …
